note.headline: Chip stocks sink Nasdaq while grains and financials hit highs
note.standfirst: Nvidia's -4.57% drop dragged the semiconductor complex lower and pulled the Nasdaq 100 down -0.70%, even as Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Netflix posted broad gains. Small caps and mid caps sold off far harder than large caps, and credit softened alongside a firmer dollar, leaving the split between chip hardware and megacap software as the session's central question.
takeaways: Nvidia's -4.57% drop led a chip-sector retreat that pulled the Nasdaq 100 down -0.70% despite gains in Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Netflix.
Small caps and mid caps underperformed large caps by a wide margin, off -1.39% and -1.20% respectively against a slim -0.25% loss for large caps.
The Treasury curve shifted up roughly 1bp across the belly and long end, holding 2s10s at 47bp and 5s30s at 81bp while 3m10y widened +2bp to 83bp.
The dollar index rose +0.52% to 99.68 as USD/TRY and the grain complex, corn, wheat and soybeans, pushed to session highs.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms a rotation inside technology rather than a broad tech unwind. Technology fell -1.55% on Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, but communications rose +1.42% and consumer discretionary rose +1.15% on the back of Amazon, Alphabet, Netflix and Microsoft. Breadth stayed positive, 16 advancers against 9 decliners, so the index-level softness in large caps sat on top of a market that was not broadly selling. The gap opened where leverage to hardware capex met leverage to platform earnings, and today the market paid for the latter and sold the former.

The level that decides whether this stays contained is the 10-year yield at 4.67%, up about 1bp on the day inside a broad parallel shift. Credit already leans soft, LQD and HYG both closed at session lows on the extremes list, and small caps carry the largest negative pull in the risk barometer after the dollar. The MOVE index rose +1.58% while VIX fell -0.55%, a gap between rates volatility and equity volatility that has not yet forced a repricing in stocks. If the 10-year pushes through 4.67% with conviction, that gap closes the hard way, through credit and small caps first.
watching: Whether Nvidia's -4.57% slide extends into the wider semiconductor group or stays contained to the mega-cap names that fell today.
Follow-through in LQD and HYG, both marked at session lows on the extremes list.
The dollar index at 99.68, close enough to the 100 level that a push through it would tighten financial conditions further.
The gap between the MOVE index, up +1.58% to 70.965, and VIX, down -0.55% to 14.43.
note.equities:
Large caps closed little changed against a much softer small and mid-cap tape. The broad index fell -0.25%, the Nasdaq 100 fell -0.70%, the Dow was flat at -0.02%, small caps fell -1.39%, mid caps fell -1.20% and the NYSE Composite fell -0.26%. The gap between large and small is the story: nothing in the mega-cap complex broke down enough to explain a -1.39% day in small caps on its own.

Sector rotation ran straight through technology. XLK fell -1.55% on Nvidia (-4.57%), AMD (-2.33%), Broadcom (-0.74%) and Oracle (-0.72%), while communications rose +1.42% and consumer discretionary rose +1.15% on Amazon (+3.97%), Netflix (+2.35%), Alphabet (+1.74%) and Microsoft (+1.68%). Financials added +0.38% with Bank of America up +1.88%. Breadth held positive at 16 advancers to 9 decliners, a 1.78 ratio, with dispersion at 1.66, consistent with a market rotating between winners rather than one selling in bulk.
note.rates:
The curve moved up in a parallel shift of roughly 1bp across the 2-year, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year, leaving the shape unchanged. 2s10s held at 47bp and 5s30s held at 81bp, both flat on the day, while 3m10y widened +2bp to 83bp. Levels: 2-year at 4.20%, 5-year at 4.38%, 10-year at 4.67%, 30-year at 5.19%.

Breakevens compressed while real yields held. The 5-year breakeven fell 1bp to 2.30%, the 10-year fell 2bp to 2.31%, and the 5y5y forward fell 3bp to 2.32%, while 10-year TIPS were unchanged at 2.34%. That is a market paying up for real duration and trimming inflation compensation, not a market repricing the growth outlook.
note.credit: Credit softened across the board with investment grade underperforming high yield: LQD fell -0.36%, HYG fell -0.16%, JNK fell -0.17%, EM sovereign debt
